subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Lake Saiful Muluk is located in the:
explanation: Lake Saiful Muluk lies above Naran in the Kaghan Valley of Mansehra district.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The largest freshwater lake in Pakistan is:
explanation: Manchar Lake near Sehwan in Jamshoro district is fed by the Indus and hill torrents from the Kirthar Range.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Satpara Lake is situated near:
explanation: Satpara Lake lies just south of Skardu in Baltistan and has been raised by the Satpara Dam.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Attabad Lake in Hunza was formed in 2010 by:
o: a landslide blocking the Hunza River
explanation: A massive landslide at Attabad in January 2010 dammed the Hunza River and submerged part of the Karakoram Highway.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Hanna Lake is situated near:
explanation: Hanna Lake lies in the hills just east of Quetta and is a well-known picnic spot of the city.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Neelum Valley is located in:
explanation: The Neelum Valley runs north-east from Muzaffarabad along the Neelum River, close to the Line of Control.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Kaghan Valley is part of which district?
explanation: The Kaghan Valley, drained by the Kunhar River, lies in Mansehra district of Hazara Division.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which place is called the ‘Jewel of Hindukush’?
explanation: Chitral, surrounded by the high peaks of the Hindu Kush including Tirich Mir, is popularly called the Jewel of the Hindu Kush.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which valley is often called the ‘Switzerland of the East’?
explanation: Swat’s green valleys, rivers and snow-capped peaks have long drawn comparisons with the Alpine scenery of Switzerland.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Hingol National Park is located in:
explanation: Hingol, Pakistan’s largest national park, lies along the Makran coast in the Lasbela, Gwadar and Awaran area of Balochistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The ‘Princess of Hope’ rock formation lies in:
explanation: The wind-carved Princess of Hope and the Sphinx-like formations stand beside the Makran Coastal Highway in Hingol National Park.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Kirthar National Park is located in:
explanation: Kirthar National Park lies in the Kirthar hills in Jamshoro and Karachi districts of Sindh.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Lal Suhanra National Park is near:
explanation: Lal Suhanra, east of Bahawalpur, combines desert, forest plantation and wetland habitats on the edge of Cholistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Deosai National Park, whose name is said to mean ‘land of giants’, is in:
explanation: The high Deosai plains lie between Skardu and Astore in Gilgit-Baltistan and shelter the Himalayan brown bear.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Khunjerab National Park was established mainly to protect the:
explanation: Khunjerab National Park was created in 1975 to protect the Marco Polo sheep and snow leopard of the high Karakoram.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Margalla Hills National Park is in:
explanation: The park covers the Margalla Hills, Rawal Lake and Shakarparian on the northern side of Islamabad.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Chitral Gol National Park is best known for protecting the:
explanation: Chitral Gol, next to Chitral town, holds one of the largest populations of the Kashmir markhor, Pakistan’s national animal.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Indus Dolphin Reserve lies on the stretch of river between:
explanation: The blind Indus dolphin is concentrated in the Indus between the Guddu and Sukkur barrages, declared a reserve in 1974.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Most of Pakistan’s rainfall comes from the:
explanation: The monsoon brings heavy rain to Punjab, Kashmir and the upper Khyber Pakhtunkhwa between July and September.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Winter rain in north and west Pakistan is caused mainly by:
explanation: Low-pressure systems from the Mediterranean region, called western disturbances, bring winter rain and snow to the north and west.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The hot, dry, dusty wind that blows over the Punjab plains in summer is called the:
explanation: The Loo blows across the plains of Pakistan and northern India in May and June, raising afternoon temperatures sharply.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The climate of most of Pakistan is:
explanation: Apart from the northern mountains and the sub-montane belt, most of Pakistan receives little rain, with large areas getting under 250 mm a year.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The earthquake of 8 October 2005 had its epicentre near:
explanation: The magnitude 7.6 earthquake was centred near Muzaffarabad and devastated Azad Kashmir and the Hazara areas, including Balakot.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The city largely destroyed by an earthquake in 1935 was:
explanation: The Quetta earthquake of 31 May 1935 killed tens of thousands and flattened most of the city.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Kharif crops are sown in:
explanation: Kharif crops such as rice, cotton and maize are sown at the start of the hot season and harvested in autumn.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which of the following is a Rabi crop?
explanation: Rabi crops are sown in October–December and harvested in spring; wheat is the main Rabi crop, while rice, cotton and maize are Kharif crops.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which of the following is a Kharif crop?
explanation: Rice is sown in the summer monsoon season, whereas wheat, gram and barley are winter (Rabi) crops.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Rabi crops in Pakistan are generally harvested in:
explanation: Rabi crops sown in winter ripen in spring; wheat harvesting in Punjab and Sindh takes place mainly in April and May.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The staple food crop of Pakistan is:
explanation: Wheat flour is the basic food of most Pakistanis and wheat occupies the largest cropped area in the country.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which crop is the main raw material of Pakistan’s textile industry?
explanation: Cotton lint feeds the spinning and weaving mills that make textiles Pakistan’s largest manufacturing and export sector.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Districts such as Multan, Bahawalpur and Rahim Yar Khan are best known for growing:
explanation: The hot, irrigated plains of southern Punjab form the core of Pakistan’s cotton belt, along with parts of Sindh.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s aromatic Basmati rice comes mainly from the ______ tract of Punjab.
explanation: The Kalar tract around Gujranwala, Sialkot, Sheikhupura and Hafizabad has the soil and climate suited to Basmati.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In Pakistan, ‘barani’ land means land that is:
explanation: Barani areas, such as much of the Potohar Plateau, depend on rainfall rather than canals for their crops.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which district is famous for its Kinnow oranges?
explanation: Sargodha is the heart of Pakistan’s citrus belt and produces most of the Kinnow mandarins exported by the country.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Khairpur in Sindh is famous for the production of:
explanation: Khairpur is one of Pakistan’s main date-growing districts; Turbat and Panjgur in Balochistan are also known for dates.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Tobacco in Pakistan is grown mainly in the districts of:
explanation: The Peshawar valley districts of Mardan and Swabi in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa produce most of Pakistan’s flue-cured Virginia tobacco.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Sindhri variety of mango is especially associated with:
explanation: Sindhri, one of Pakistan’s best-known export mangoes, is grown chiefly around Mirpur Khas in Sindh.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The largest sub-sector of Pakistan’s agriculture by value added is:
explanation: For many years livestock has contributed more than half of agricultural value added, ahead of major and minor crops.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The ‘Green Revolution’ in Pakistan’s agriculture took place in the:
explanation: High-yielding wheat and rice varieties, fertilisers and tube-wells sharply raised output under Ayub Khan in the 1960s.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited was formerly known as the:
explanation: The Agricultural Development Bank of Pakistan was converted into ZTBL in 2002; it remains the main public lender to farmers.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Ayub Agricultural Research Institute is located in:
explanation: The institute in Faisalabad is Punjab’s main centre for developing crop varieties and farming techniques.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s largest export sector is:
explanation: Textiles and garments have long earned more than half of Pakistan’s merchandise export receipts.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Faisalabad is called the ‘Manchester of Pakistan’ because of its:
explanation: Like Manchester in England, Faisalabad is dominated by spinning, weaving and garment mills.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Sialkot is famous for manufacturing:
explanation: Sialkot exports footballs and other sports goods and is also a major centre of surgical instrument making.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The city of Gujrat is best known for manufacturing:
explanation: Gujrat in Punjab is Pakistan’s main centre of electric fan manufacturing, and is also known for pottery and furniture.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Wazirabad is famous for:
explanation: Wazirabad in Gujranwala district has a long tradition of knife-making and cutlery.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Hyderabad (Sindh) is famous for its:
explanation: Hyderabad’s cottage industry produces most of the glass bangles sold in Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Chiniot is famous for its:
explanation: Chiniot craftsmen are renowned for elaborately carved wooden furniture and woodwork.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan Steel Mills is located at:
explanation: Pakistan Steel Mills stands at Bin Qasim near Karachi, close to Port Qasim for imports of iron ore and coal.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan Steel Mills was built with the assistance of the:
explanation: The Soviet Union financed and designed Pakistan Steel Mills, whose construction began in the 1970s.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Heavy Mechanical Complex at Taxila was set up with the assistance of:
explanation: The Heavy Mechanical Complex was established in the early 1970s with Chinese help to manufacture industrial machinery.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Most urea fertiliser in Pakistan is manufactured using:
explanation: Natural gas is both the feedstock and the fuel of Pakistan’s urea plants, which is why gas shortages affect fertiliser output.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s first Export Processing Zone was established at:
explanation: The Karachi Export Processing Zone, set up in 1980 at Landhi, was the country’s first zone offering export-oriented incentives.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: CPEC stands for:
explanation: CPEC is a package of energy, transport and industrial projects linking Pakistan and China.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: CPEC is a flagship project of China’s:
explanation: CPEC is regarded as the flagship corridor of the Belt and Road Initiative announced by China in 2013.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: CPEC links Gwadar Port with the Chinese city of:
explanation: The corridor runs from Gwadar on the Arabian Sea through Pakistan and over the Khunjerab Pass to Kashgar in Xinjiang.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which CPEC special economic zone is located in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
explanation: The Rashakai SEZ lies near Nowshera on the M-1 motorway; Dhabeji is in Sindh, Allama Iqbal Industrial City in Punjab and Bostan in Balochistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Allama Iqbal Industrial City, a CPEC special economic zone, is near:
explanation: The zone, developed by the Faisalabad Industrial Estate Development and Management Company, is one of the priority SEZs under CPEC.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Dhabeji Special Economic Zone is located in:
explanation: Dhabeji lies in Thatta district, east of Karachi, close to Port Qasim.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Since 2013, Gwadar Port has been operated by:
explanation: Operation of Gwadar Port passed from Singapore’s PSA to the China Overseas Port Holding Company in 2013.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s largest and busiest seaport is:
explanation: Karachi Port, on the natural harbour of Kiamari, handles the largest share of Pakistan’s sea trade.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Port Muhammad bin Qasim is located near:
explanation: Port Qasim, Pakistan’s second major port, lies in the creeks east of Karachi.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s first motorway, the M-2, connects Lahore with:
explanation: The Lahore–Islamabad M-2 opened in 1997 as the first motorway in South Asia.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Sialkot–Lahore Motorway is designated:
explanation: The M-11 links Lahore with the export city of Sialkot; M-5 is Multan–Sukkur and M-9 Karachi–Hyderabad.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Karachi–Hyderabad Motorway is designated:
explanation: The M-9 runs between Karachi and Hyderabad in Sindh, replacing the old Super Highway.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Karakoram Highway is also designated as:
explanation: The KKH is National Highway 35, running from Hasan Abdal to the Khunjerab Pass; N-5 is the Karachi–Torkham highway.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Karakoram Highway links Pakistan with China’s region of:
explanation: The highway crosses the Khunjerab Pass into Xinjiang and continues to Kashgar.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: National Highway N-5 runs from Karachi to:
explanation: The N-5, Pakistan’s longest national highway, follows the Indus plain and the old Grand Trunk Road to Torkham on the Afghan border.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Makran Coastal Highway connects Karachi with:
explanation: The Makran Coastal Highway (N-10) runs along the Balochistan coast from near Karachi to Gwadar.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan Railways’ Main Line-1 (ML-1) runs between:
explanation: ML-1, the backbone of the network, links Karachi with Peshawar via Hyderabad, Multan, Lahore and Rawalpindi; its upgrade is part of CPEC.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The headquarters of Pakistan Railways is in:
explanation: Pakistan Railways is headquartered in Lahore, a legacy of the North Western Railway.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s first metro rail line, the Orange Line, operates in:
explanation: The Orange Line Metro Train in Lahore, built under CPEC, began commercial operations in 2020.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Kohat Tunnel on the Indus Highway was built with assistance from:
explanation: Japanese financing and engineering helped build the Kohat Tunnel, which opened in 2003 between Peshawar and Kohat.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s dry port on the Karakoram Highway near the Chinese border is at:
explanation: Sost in Upper Hunza is the customs and immigration post for traffic crossing the Khunjerab Pass.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Monetary policy in Pakistan is formulated by the:
explanation: As the central bank, the State Bank of Pakistan sets the policy interest rate and regulates credit and money supply.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The State Bank of Pakistan was inaugurated on:
explanation: Quaid-i-Azam inaugurated the State Bank in Karachi on 1 July 1948, one of his last public engagements.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan was:
explanation: Zahid Hussain, a former Indian civil servant, headed the State Bank from 1948 to 1953.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The head office of the State Bank of Pakistan is in:
explanation: The State Bank has remained headquartered in Karachi, the country’s financial centre, since 1948.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Commercial banks in Pakistan were nationalised in:
explanation: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto’s government nationalised the banks on 1 January 1974; privatisation began in the early 1990s.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Habib Bank, which moved its head office to Karachi in 1947, was founded in 1941 in:
explanation: Habib Bank was established in Bombay in 1941 and shifted to Karachi at Quaid-i-Azam’s request after independence.
